title: From constrained movement to parallel gradients

sections.title: Constrained movement on the level set
sections.body: Consider a smooth objective f(x,y) and a constraint g(x,y)=c whose level set is a regular curve. At a feasible point the admissible infinitesimal displacements δr satisfy ∇g·δr=0. Therefore any first-order change in f along the constraint is ∇f·δr. If ∇f is not parallel to ∇g, there exists an admissible δr for which ∇f·δr≠0, so f can increase or decrease while remaining on the constraint. Only when ∇f=λ∇g for some multiplier λ is every admissible directional derivative zero. The symbols ∇, λ, δr and the identity ∇f·δr=0 are retained as disciplinary notation.

sections.title: Parallel gradients as a stationarity condition
sections.body: The multiplier equations ∇f=λ∇g together with g=c characterise constrained stationary points. They do not, by themselves, establish a global maximum or minimum: second-order or boundary analysis may still be required. Feasibility of (x*,y*) on g=c and vanishing of first-order constrained variation are necessary for an interior constrained extremum under standard smoothness assumptions.

sections.title: Worked algebraic sketch
sections.body: Example. Let f(x,y)=x²+y² and g(x,y)=x+y with c=1. Then ∇f=(2x,2y) and ∇g=(1,1). Parallelism requires 2x=λ and 2y=λ, hence x=y, and with x+y=1 we obtain x=y=½, λ=1. The candidate (½,½) is feasible and stationary for the constrained problem.

sections.title: What the equations establish — and do not
sections.body: The system establishes a constrained stationary candidate. It does not automatically certify that the candidate is a constrained minimum of f on the whole level set; comparing values or using a second-derivative test on the constraint is a further justification step.

sections.title: Unsupported inference to watch for
sections.body: An unsupported inference would claim that solving ∇f=λ∇g and g=c alone proves a global constrained extremum without additional argument. Distinguish constrained stationarity from an established extremum.

sections.title: Geometric reading
sections.body: Geometrically, level curves of f are tangent to the constraint curve when gradients are parallel. Tangency is the geometric face of ∇f=λ∇g. Movement along the constraint cannot raise or lower f to first order at such a point.

sections.title: Continuity into materials
sections.body: Subsequent materials should ask learners to formulate multiplier equations, solve a small system, and evaluate what the solution establishes. Prefer performing the algebra and structured judgements over writing about how one would perform them.
